text:
Nine days after San Jose beat them 6-2 in Ottawa, the Senators returned the favor in the Sharks' own building, and they did it with the kind of night that leaves no argument. Ottawa scored four straight after Michael Misa tied it late in the first, pulling away in the second period with goals from Drake Batherson, Tim Stützle and Ridly Greig, whose came shorthanded.

Our numbers say the score fit the game. Ottawa generated 3.83 expected goals (a measure of the quality of chances) to San Jose's 1.73, took 80 shot attempts to 42, and deserved to win about 81 percent of the time, which is the share of simulated replays of every shot that Ottawa wins. The Senators got stronger as it went, out-chancing the Sharks 1.68 to 0.69 in the third. Stützle, drafted third overall in 2020 out of Adler Mannheim, took seven shots on goal and finished with a goal and an assist. Dylan Cozens opened the scoring on a 3 percent chance, then added an assist.

Samuel Ersson stopped 22 of 23 shots, a bit better than the chances he faced called for. At the other end, Alex Nedeljkovic allowed four on 34 shots, about what the shots deserved, so this was not a goalie being left to fend for himself so much as a team getting buried in front of him. San Jose also took 18 penalty minutes to Ottawa's eight, though neither side scored on the power play. The Sharks answer for the first-period equalizer and not much more, and they have the season series split at one win each. Ottawa leaves with the cleaner evidence of which team was better on the night.
